A separate per-revision 'effective key' is rebuilt when the registry changes, and values go into an LRU byte cache under (effective key, raw scale). The within() placeholder is an internal identity op bound to the base, so the sub-pipeline is an ordinary keyed subgraph that never shares nodes with the same pipeline written directly.

A.worst_thing: Keying an argument by object identity or repr (grid.py:87-91): the stale-by-source-text failure the chapter warns about, in a new form.

A neutral identity is folded at build time, so gain(k=1) simply is its input node.

generativity.notes: C, D and E share one deep structure: canonical text, SHA-256 node hash, a separate per-request signature, run memo, quantised scale, substitution for within. They differ in where implementation identity lives (C node hash, D signature serial, E version only) and in how they deal with depth (C changes the global recursion limit at import, D raises it per request, E walks iteratively). A and B share a leaner shape: tuple keys, raw scale, no memo, a placeholder bound to the base. They differ in neutral handling (A at eval, double-charged; B folded at build) and in invalidation (A gen token, B cache wipe). Every implementation reproduced the cache-entry-with-warnings seam. Each one aggregated subgraph warnings differently, and three of the five get diamonds or repeated text wrong.

worse_is_better: B comes closest to the same observable quality for this interface with the least machinery. Its keys are small tuples over one 128-bit content digest with a collision check, a neutral call folds away at build time, and there is no signature layer. C, D and E add a second SHA-256 signature computed per node per request (a recomputed hash chain over a graph whose node hashes are already structural), canonical-text modules, coded error hierarchies, and in D a tentative-scaffolding system. Two of these extras are needed: refusing callables and quantising the scale are each a few lines B could add. The per-request signature walk and D's hole machinery are not needed, because an in-process cache keyed by (node hash, registration serial, quantised scale) is equivalent. B's real gaps are small and local: the repr/identity fallback for arguments, the raw scale, and the cache wipe on every op().
chapter_lessons: Say that the key must identify the registration, not only the declared version. E keyed on version only and serves the old function after an in-process replacement (impl-E/gridflow/engine.py:282). A and D added a serial (impl-A/gridflow/ops.py:49, impl-D/gridflow/ops.py:60), B wiped the cache, and C froze the old record into existing nodes.

Say how to aggregate warnings across a subgraph. 'Store with the value, report once per evaluation' produced duplicates on diamonds (impl-A/gridflow/engine.py:231, impl-C/gridflow/engine.py:343-349) and text-dedup that drops distinct sources (B, D). E's per-request reported set (impl-E/gridflow/engine.py:85-89) is the shape to recommend.

The separate Signature participant teaches too much for an in-process cache. Three implementations recompute a SHA-256 chain over the whole reachable graph on every request even when the root is cached (impl-C/gridflow/engine.py:247, impl-D/gridflow/engine.py:316, impl-E/gridflow/engine.py:305). Say that the signature is (node hash, registration id, quantised params) and can be memoised per node and parameter set.

Graph depth is a missing force. C, D and E each fought recursion differently (import-time global, per-request limit change, iterative walk), and E's iterative rewrite lost the top-down cache cut-off (impl-E/gridflow/engine.py:306-309). State the law 'look up the root before descending' explicitly.

The placeholder sketch is ambiguous. D documents the constant-hash trap and builds scaffolding to escape it (impl-D/gridflow/node.py:25-31); C shows that one shared hole object plus substitution is enough; A and B bound the hole to the base and lost sharing. Show the substitution step and its re-interning.

Mark the in-flight group and parallel inputs as optional for single-threaded hosts (D and E argued them away in docstrings), and offer build-time folding of argument-only identities (impl-B/gridflow/engine.py:202-204) as a simpler alternative to copy-on-neutral when values are immutable.
